text: A network has the address 192.168.10.0/26. What is the maximum number of usable host addresses in this subnet?
solution_text: With a /26 mask, 32 - 26 = 6 bits are left for hosts. Total addresses = 2^6 = 64. Subtracting the network and broadcast addresses gives 62 usable hosts.

text: A stop-and-wait protocol is used on a link of bandwidth 1 Mbps with a one-way propagation delay of 20 ms. The frame size is 1000 bytes and the ACK size is negligible. What is the link utilization (efficiency)?
solution_text: Transmission time Tt = 8000 bits / 10^6 bps = 8 ms. Efficiency = Tt / (Tt + 2*Tp) = 8 / (8 + 40) = 1/6, which is about 16.67%.

text: A router has the forwarding table entries: 10.0.0.0/8 -> R1, 10.1.0.0/16 -> R2, 10.1.2.0/24 -> R3, 0.0.0.0/0 -> R4. To which next hop will a packet with destination address 10.1.2.7 be forwarded?
solution_text: 10.1.2.7 matches 10.0.0.0/8, 10.1.0.0/16, 10.1.2.0/24 and the default route. Routers use the longest prefix match, so the /24 entry wins and the packet goes to R3.

text: A TCP sender starts with cwnd = 1 MSS in the 1st transmission round and ssthresh = 16 MSS. There is no packet loss. Assuming cwnd doubles per round in slow start and grows by 1 MSS per round in congestion avoidance, what is the cwnd (in MSS) in the 7th transmission round?
solution_text: Rounds 1 to 5 give cwnd = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. At 16 = ssthresh, slow start ends and linear growth begins. Round 6 gives 17 and round 7 gives 18.

text: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to map:

options.A: An IP address to a MAC address
options.B: A MAC address to an IP address
options.C: A domain name to an IP address
options.D: A port number to an IP address

solution_text: ARP finds the MAC (hardware) address that corresponds to a known IP address on the local network. The reverse mapping was done by RARP, and domain name resolution is done by DNS.

text: Which of the following statements about CSMA/CD in Ethernet are TRUE?

options.A: The transmission time of a frame must be at least twice the one-way propagation delay
options.B: After the k-th collision, a station picks a random backoff slot from 0 to 2^k - 1 (with a cap on k)
options.C: CSMA/CD is required in full-duplex switched Ethernet
options.D: If the bandwidth is increased while the frame size and cable length stay the same, collision detection still works

solution_text: A is true because the sender must still be transmitting when the collision signal returns (Tt >= 2*Tp). B is true because it is binary exponential backoff. C is false because full-duplex links have no collisions. D is false because higher bandwidth reduces Tt, so Tt < 2*Tp may result.

text: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation are TRUE?

options.A: Reassembly of fragments is done only at the destination host
options.B: The fragment offset field is measured in units of 8 bytes
options.C: The More Fragments (MF) bit is 0 in the last fragment
options.D: Intermediate routers reassemble fragments before forwarding them

solution_text: In IPv4, fragments are reassembled only at the destination. The offset is in 8-byte units and MF = 0 marks the last fragment. Intermediate routers do not reassemble, so D is false.

text: Which of the following statements about routing protocols are TRUE?

options.A: Distance vector routing can suffer from the count-to-infinity problem
options.B: OSPF is a link-state routing protocol
options.C: RIP uses Dijkstra's algorithm to compute routes
options.D: In link-state routing, every router builds a view of the complete network topology

solution_text: Distance vector protocols (e.g. RIP) can count to infinity. OSPF is link-state, and every router floods link state and builds the full topology map. RIP is distance vector (Bellman-Ford), so C is false.

text: A sliding window protocol is used on a link with bandwidth 2 Mbps and one-way propagation delay 18 ms. The frame size is 1000 bytes. What is the minimum window size (in frames) needed to achieve 100% link utilization? Ignore ACK transmission time.
solution_text: Tt = 8000 / (2 x 10^6) = 4 ms. Tp = 18 ms. Window size W = 1 + 2*Tp/Tt = 1 + 36/4 = 10 frames.
